counterfactual_missing_items: no raw evidence of neutropenia; the WBC count is 25,000 with 85% neutrophils
no raw peritoneal signs that would suggest free perforation rather than a localized collection
no culture or aspirate of the pericecal collection is reported
decisive_items: a swollen and thickened tubular structure measuring 36 × 27 mm at the cecal pole, with a 25‐mm pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips
a laparoscopic appendectomy performed 8 months earlier
pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
response.rationale: R4 is the most complete: the raw CT span explicitly couples the swollen, thickened tubular cecal pole with a pericecal collection, identifying complicated appendiceal disease/abscess. R5 uses the same tubular structure but omits the collection and the prior appendectomy, making it less specific. R6 is counterfactual because neutropenic colitis requires neutropenia, whereas the vignette shows a high neutrophil-predominant WBC count.

rejected.why: Neutropenic colitis is contradicted by leukocytosis with 85% neutrophils and by the pericecal collection and prior appendectomy, which are better explained by appendiceal abscess.
